title: Backgrounds, borders and shadows
summary: Add background colours, rounded corners and soft shadows to make boxes look like cards and buttons.

quiz.q: Which property gives a box rounded corners?
quiz.explain: `border-radius` rounds the corners. A larger value means a rounder corner.

quiz.q: How do you turn a square element into a circle?
quiz.explain: A radius of 50% rounds each corner by half of the side, so a square becomes a circle. On a non-square element you get an ellipse.

quiz.q: Fill the shadow so it moves 0 right, 4px down, and blurs by 8px.
quiz.explain: `box-shadow` is x-offset, y-offset, blur radius, optional spread, then colour. A positive y-offset moves the shadow down.

quiz.q: The author wants a shadow under the card, but it never appears. Click the faulty line.
quiz.explain: The colon is missing after `box-shadow`. When one declaration is broken the browser skips just that line.

exercise.task:
Turn the boxes into a card and an avatar. Work in `index.html`.

- `.card`: `background-color` of `whitesmoke`, `border-radius` of 12px, a `1px solid` border, and a `box-shadow`.
- `.avatar`: `width` and `height` of 80px, `background-color` of `steelblue`, and `border-radius: 50%` to make it a circle.
hints: Backgrounds, corners and shadows each have their own property.
A shadow needs offsets, a blur and a colour, for example `0 4px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3)`.

checks.name: .avatar is 80px by 80px
checks.hint: Give .avatar a width and a height of 80px.
